{{legend0|#808080|No votes}} | title = [[Governor of Vermont|Governor]] | before_election = [[Phil Scott]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Phil Scott]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) | turnout = 72.12% ({{gain}} 14.50 pp) }} {{Elections in Vermont}} The '''2024 Vermont gubernatorial election''' was held on November 5, 2024, to elect the [[List of governors of Vermont|governor of Vermont]], concurrently with the [[2024 United States presidential election|2024 U.S. presidential election]], as well as [[United States Senate elections, 2024|elections]] to the [[United States Senate]] and elections to the [[United States House of Representatives]] and various [[2024 United States elections#State elections|state]] and local elections. Incumbent [[Vermont Republican Party|Republican]] governor [[Phil Scott]] won re-election to a fifth term, defeating the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] nominee, [[Vermont Commission on Women]] co-chair [[Esther Charlestin]].{{Cite web |author=Kinzel, Bob |date=2023-10-19 |title=If Gov. Phil Scott runs for reelection, he will remain a Republican |url=https://www.vermontpublic.org/local-news/2023-10-19/if-gov-phil-scott-runs-for-re-election-he-will-remain-a-republican |access-date=2023-11-13 |website=Vermont Public |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Mearhoff |first=Sarah |date=2024-08-13 |title=Esther Charlestin wins Democratic gubernatorial nod while statewide incumbents cruise to primary victories |url=https://vtdigger.org/2024/08/13/most-of-vermonts-statewide-incumbents-cruise-to-easy-primary-victories-tuesday/ |access-date=2024-11-03 |website=VTDigger |language=en-US}}{{cite news|last=Thomas|first=Steff Danielle|date=November 5, 2024|url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/4967738-phil-scott-vermont-governor/|title=GOP Gov. Phil Scott wins reelection in blue Vermont|work=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]]|access-date=November 17, 2024}} Primary elections took place on August 13, 2024.{{Cite web |title=2024 State Primary Election Dates |url=https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2024-state-primary-election-dates |access-date=2023-08-06 |website=www.ncsl.org}} Being frequently ranked as the nation's most popular governor,{{Cite web |date=2023-07-24 |title=Poll finds Scott retains highest approval rating among governors in US |url=https://www.wcax.com/2023/07/24/poll-finds-scott-retains-highest-approval-rating-among-governors-us/ |access-date=2024-03-16 |website=WCAX News |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Mueller |first=Julia |date=2023-01-12 |title=Here are America’s most popular and least popular governors |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/state-watch/3811233-here-are-americas-most-popular-and-least-popular-governors/ |access-date=2024-03-16 |website=The Hill |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last=MultiState |title=Decoding 2023 Gubernatorial Approval Ratings |url=https://www.multistate.us/insider/2023/8/4/decoding-2023-gubernatorial-approval-ratings |access-date=2024-03-16 |website=MultiState |language=en-US}} Scott has won re-election by continually increasing margins since his first election in 2016. Despite Vermont's strong Democratic lean at the presidential level, Scott was expected to easily win again in 2024. Along with [[2024 New Hampshire gubernatorial election|New Hampshire]], this race was one of two Republican-held governorships up for election in 2024 in a state carried by [[Joe Biden]] in the [[2020 United States presidential election in Vermont|2020 presidential election]]. This was the best Republican performance in a Vermont gubernatorial election since [[1946 Vermont gubernatorial election|1946]], with Scott winning every municipality (as he did in [[2022 Vermont gubernatorial election|2022]]){{cite web |last1=McDonald |first1=Zoe |title=Vermont election updates: Scott, Rodgers and legislative candidates give strong showing |url=https://www.vermontpublic.org/live-updates/vermont-election-results-november-2024 |website=Vermont Public |access-date=17 November 2024}} and Scott's coattails allowed Republicans to break Democratic supermajorities in the state legislature. Scott also achieved over 60% of the vote in [[Windham County, Vermont|Windham County]], a traditionally Democratic stronghold. {{toclimit|3}} ==Republican primary== ===Candidates=== ====Nominee====
